correctness.rationale: For a color-exchanging involution, invariant faces consist of vertex orbits, and independence number at most two permits at most two orbits. The four-vertex induced bipartite subgraph has independence number at most two exactly when it has a perfect matching; these are precisely the off-diagonal orbit edges or two diagonal edges, giving the PL graph Q union \(K_L\). Connectedness follows from the quotient of connected G. The root-bridged bipartite double cover of any connected H is connected, has Q=H and singleton L, and so realizes H exactly. A triangle-fan argument directly proves the ambient \(\pi_1\) vanishes. Complete finite checks of 1,098 small symmetric adjacency matrices and 772 connected lifts corroborate the independent-triple criterion; they are not the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: A natural class of color-exchanging involutions receives an exact PL fixed-space classification rather than only Euler or Betti data. The inverse rooted-cover construction realizes each connected graph as the fixed locus inside a simply connected robust clique complex, a structural universality phenomenon that is not implied by the ambient three-sphere-wedge or equivariant-character formulas. The result has concrete uses for constructing group actions with prescribed fixed fundamental group and explaining why ambient simple connectivity need not pass to fixed loci.
